Application Materials.content:
When you apply you’ll need to submit a personal statement explaining why you want to take the course. You’ll need to include information about:
- your knowledge of the subject area
- why you want to study a postgraduate qualification in this course
- how you intend to use your qualification
References are not required for this programme. Please include the required paperwork showing your first degree and your IELTS English language test score (if you are a non-native English speaker) with your application. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Application Deadlines.content:
**Data and Decision Analytics (MSc)** starts **September 2026** for **1 year**.
Application deadlines:
- **International students:** The deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 19 August 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.
- **UK students:** The deadline to apply for this course is **Wednesday 2 September 2026, midday UK time**. Applications may close before the expected deadline if places are filled.

Academic Requirements.content:
You'll need a **2:1 degree in a quantitative subject** with an appropriate level (**2:1 or equivalent**) for your Mathematics modules, which must form a substantial part of your degree. Find the [equivalent international qualifications](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/uni-life/international/your-country.page) for your country.
For China applicants: Southampton accepts bachelor's degrees (学士学位) from China. To apply, you'll usually need the equivalent of a **2:1** undergraduate degree from a highly ranked Chinese university, with a minimum average grade depending on the university where you studied. Each institution falls into one of 4 groups called 'tiers'; if your institution isn't listed, use the grades for tier D.
| China institution tier | 2:1 equivalent GPA out of 4.0 | GPA out of 5.0 | Percentage (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier A | **2.8** | **3.5** | **70%** |
| Tier B | **3.1** | **3.88** | **75%** |
| Tier C | **3.25** | **4.06** | **80%** |
| Tier D | **3.7** | **4.63** | **88%** |

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must show that you can use English to the level required. [Visit the English language pages](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentadmin/admissions/admissions-policies/language.page) to find out which qualifications are accepted and how you can meet the requirements.
If taking IELTS, you must get at least:
| IELTS component | Minimum score |
| --- | --- |
| Overall | **6.5** |
| Reading | **6.0** |
| Writing | **6.0** |
| Speaking | **6.0** |
| Listening | **6.0** |
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of the [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) before starting the course.
When applying, include the required paperwork showing your IELTS English language test score if you are a non-native English speaker. Without these, your application may be delayed.

Program Overview.content:
Data and Decision Analytics (MSc) is a Master of Science course starting September 2026, lasting 1 year, delivered full-time at Highfield campus. This qualification is awarded by the University of Southampton.
Develop the analytic and professional skills for success in data science on this Data & Decision Analytics MSc. You’ll learn advanced level mathematical modelling, statistical analysis, and computation. This UK master’s course will give you the skills and knowledge to make better decisions based on data. There is also a strong focus on real work experience, with opportunities for summer projects in a range of industries.
Through this degree you’ll learn:
- programming skills in R and in Python
- advanced theory and methods of applied statistics
- practical application of operational research
- modelling of deterministic and stochastic systems
- industry career skills working on a project with an external organisation
You'll take on a 3-month summer project which can be in operational research, statistics, data science or a combination of each. This is excellent preparation if you want to go onto a PhD in one of these areas. There are 2 options for this project:
- The opportunity to compete for a 3-month project with an external organisation
- An internal project linked to the latest research led by one of our academics
You'll also get the chance to meet with the CORMSIS Business Advisory Board which is represented by major companies including Tesco, Shell, British Airways and [HM Revenue & Customs](http://www.hmrc.gov.uk/). They ensure this MSc continues to be fresh and relevant to the needs of employers, so you’ll have excellent employment prospects.
Professor Alain Zemkoho is your course leader. Read [Professor Zemkoho’s profile](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xd5hn/professor-alain-zemkoho) to learn more about his work.
This course is based at [Highfield](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/student-life/campuses/highfield).
This is a full-time MSc which runs over 12-months from September to the following September. There are 2 semesters of taught material. You’ll then complete an MSc project, usually in the summer. In semesters 1 and 2 you'll study a combination of modules that everyone on the course must study, and additional modules you'll get to choose from a range of options. These will provide you with the necessary foundations in operational research and statistics.
The learning activities for this course include careers talks from external organisations, employability skills training, computer programming, collecting and analysing data, using IT for optimisation, simulation, and statistical software, coursework, and individual and group projects. Assessment includes coursework and essays, a dissertation, group essays, individual and group projects, and written exams. You'll need to submit a dissertation on your project work soon after the end of the taught period of study.
This degree will allow you to develop and evidence subject-specific and targeted employability skills, including the required skill set for a range of future careers, further study, or starting your own business. The skills you can expect to focus on and gain from this course include research, critical thinking, self-management, communication, and problem solving.
Graduates commonly work in a range of organisations or sectors including Education, Engineering, Finance, Banking, Accountancy, Government, Insurance, IT, Business consultancy, Marketing, Market research, Health, and Research. Careers directly related to this course include Data analyst, Data engineer, Data scientist, Data consultant, Operational researcher, Market researcher, Management consultant, Systems analyst, Statistician, and Quantitative analyst.
Example job titles of Southampton MSc Data and Decision Analytics graduates include Data scientist, Software engineer, Data analyst, Algorithm developer, Business consultant, Data architect, Data warehouse engineer, Head of data, Financial systems officer, and Systems analyst.
Job prospects for MSc Data and Decision Analytics graduates: £33k average professional salary; 93% in a skilled profession or further study; 98% graduate employment rate. Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

Curriculum.content:
**Data and Decision Analytics (MSc)** starting **September 2026** is a **full-time** MSc for **1 year**, based at **Highfield** campus. This is a full-time MSc which runs over **12-months from September to the following September**. There are **2 semesters of taught material**. You’ll then complete an **MSc project** (usually in the summer). In semesters 1 and 2 you'll study a combination of modules that everyone on the course must study, and additional modules you'll get to choose from a range of options. These will provide you with the necessary foundations in operational research and statistics.
You'll take on **3-month summer project** which can be in operational research, statistics, data science or a combination of each. There are 2 options for this project:
- The opportunity to compete for a **3-month project with an external organisation**
- An internal project linked to the latest research led by one of our academics
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules you **must study** are:
- [**Computational Machine Learning and Optimisation**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6184)
- [**Data Mining and Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6183)
- [**Introduction to Python**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6005)
- [**OR Methods for Data Scientists**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6194)
- [**Statistical Computing in R**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6191)
- [**Statistical Methods for OR Modelling**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6006)
You **must also choose from** the following modules:
- [**Analytical Consultancy Skills**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6119)
- [**Design of Experiments**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6027)
- [**Financial Portfolio Theory**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6017)
- [**Flexible Regression**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6169)
- [**Forecasting**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6011)
- [**Machine Learning**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6168)
- [**Operational Research and Data Science Case Study 1**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6185)
- [**Operational Research and Data Science Case Study 2**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6186)
- [**Project**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6001): Students are allocated a project with an external organisation or on a topic devised by a member of staff in the Operational Research or Management Sciences group at the University of Southampton.
- [**Project Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6537)
- [**Project Risk Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6143)
- [**Revenue Management**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/math6146)
Learning activities for this course include careers talks from external organisations, employability skills training, computer programming, collecting and analysing data, using IT for optimisation, simulation, and statistical software, coursework, and individual and group projects. Assessment is through coursework and essays, a dissertation, group essays, individual and group projects, and written exams. You'll need to submit a dissertation on your project work soon after the end of the taught period of study, and you'll be required to complete their work by the middle of September.

Financial Aid.content:
Southampton Mathematics Postgraduate International Scholarship: **£3000** is available to international students studying an eligible postgraduate master’s in mathematics, including [MSc Data and Decision Analytics](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/data-decision-analytics-masters-msc) 8212 (1 year).
Eligibility: to be eligible you must be an international student, have a conditional or unconditional offer to study an eligible course, and achieve a 1st or an [equivalent qualification](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/uni-life/international/your-country.page) in your undergraduate studies.
How to apply: this is a merit based scholarship. You do not need to apply. If you meet the eligibility criteria, the university will award you this scholarship and let you know by email.

Multiple Applications.content:
If you would like to apply for both taught and research programmes, please complete a separate form for each application.
If you want to apply for two taught programmes within the same Academic School please list these in order of preference as Choice 1 and Choice 2. If you want to apply for a taught programme in another School or any research programme, please fill in a separate form.
Application form, Programme of study: Choice 2 should only be entered “if it is in the same Academic School as Choice 1. If not, please fill in a second application form.” The form also asks: “Are you applying for other programmes at the University of Southampton? Yes / No. If yes, please give details.”

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
| Reasons typically accepted for deferral | Reasons not typically accepted for deferral |
|---|---|
| Bereavement due to the loss of a close family member - a parent, grandparent, guardian, sibling, son, daughter or a close personal friend. | Unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship |
| Serious illness and health problems | To undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for |
| Victim of a natural disaster | |
| Victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK | |
| Personal accident or injury of a significant nature | |
| Child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities | |
| Relevant work experience/placements/internships | |
| Military service | |
| Change of employment circumstances | |
| Unforeseen ATAS delays | |
| Unforeseen Visa delays | |

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you do not meet the English language requirements through a test or qualification, you may be able to meet them by completing one of our [pre-sessional English programmes](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/pre-sessional) **before you start your course**.
If you don’t meet direct entry requirements, you can apply to complete a Pre-Master's programme through Southampton's partnership with OnCampus. You'll progress to your chosen course after successfully completing the programme. [Find out more about Pre-Master's programmes for international students.](https://www.oncampus.global/our-study-centres/oncampus-southampton/progression-degrees)
